entries.source:
"Arc Two, mostly," Isa says. "That was where the habitation decks were. Arc One had the good machine shops, but their gravity used to cut out whenever the ore processor started."
She smiles at the memory.
"You learned to keep one hand near a railing and never put a tool down without clipping it to something. The wreck-farms supplied whatever the station couldn't make, and every broken machine became three working machines if you gave the mechanics enough time."
Isa rests the spanner against her shoulder.
"People say a place like that teaches you how to survive. Mostly, it teaches you that almost anything can be repaired if enough people are willing to hold it together."
entries.target:
"主要是第二弧，"艾萨说道。"那里是居住甲板所在的位置。第一弧虽然有设备精良的机加工车间，但每当矿石处理机启动时，那里的重力就会中断。"
她想起这段往事，露出了微笑。
"你学会了一只手要紧抓栏杆，而且绝不在将工具夹在某处之前就放下它。 残骸农场供应着空间站无法自产的一切物资，只要给机械师们足够的时间，每一台损坏的机器都能拆解出三台能用的机器。"
艾萨把扳手靠在肩上。
"人们说，那样的地方教会了你如何生存。 但最重要的是，它教会你：只要有足够多的人愿意齐心协力，几乎任何东西都能被修好。"

"Of course not."
Isa answers too quickly.
"I don't miss the recycler alarms, or the gravity failures, or food that tasted like somebody had described vegetables to a nutrient printer."
She looks past the comm pickup for a moment.
"I miss knowing every voice on the maintenance channel. I miss people shouting repair advice through three decks of open conduit. I miss knowing that if one bulkhead failed, half the Ring would arrive with welding torches before the pressure alarm finished sounding."
Her gaze returns to you.
"It's still home. This fleet is too. Don't make that expression; I'm not saying it twice."
entries.target:
"当然不是。"
艾萨回答得太快了。
"我不会错过回收器的警报，也不会错过重力系统故障，更不会错过那种尝起来就像有人向营养打印机描述了蔬菜一样的食物。"
她目光越过通讯接收器，凝视了一会儿。
"我怀念能认出维护频道里每一种声音的日子。 我怀念人们隔着三层敞开的管道大声喊出维修建议的情景。我怀念那种感觉——只要有一道隔舱壁失效，在压力警报声尚未停止之前，半个环的维修人员就会带着焊枪赶到。"
她的目光又回到了你身上。
"这里依然是家。这支舰队也是。别摆那副表情；我才不会说第二遍。"
entries.backTranslation:
" Of course not. "
Isa answered too quickly.
" I wouldn’t miss the recycler’s alarm, nor a gravity system failure, and certainly not food that tastes like someone described vegetables to a nutrition printer. "
Her gaze drifted past the comm receiver and lingered for a moment.
" I miss the days when I could recognize every single voice on the maintenance channel. I miss the sight of people shouting repair suggestions across three layers of open ductwork. I miss that feeling—wherever a bulkhead failed, half a ring’s worth of maintenance crew would rush in with their torches before the pressure alarms had even stopped. "
Her gaze returned to you.
" This is still home. So is this fleet. Don’t give me that look; I’m not going to say it again. "

entries.source:
Isa exhales.
"Badly? Weirdly?"
She turns her slate over in her hands.
"I spent most of my life wondering if Isaac Leicester was my father. I figured maybe he was some spacer. Engineer, if I was lucky. Maybe somebody who got caught in the Collapse and shoved his kid into the safest cryopod he could find."
She gives a small shrug.
"Turns out he built the hypershunts, built Gan Eden, started a religious revolution, disappeared through a Gate, and spent the rest of his life alone inside a world the size of a solar system."
A pause.
"So I've adjusted my expectations a little."
entries.target:
艾萨呼出一口气。
"很糟糕？很奇怪？"
她手里把平板翻来覆去地看。
"我大半辈子都在琢磨，艾萨克·莱斯特是不是我的父亲。我猜他可能是个太空人。如果我运气好的话，或许是个工程师。 也许是某个在崩塌中被困的人，把自己的孩子塞进了他能找到的最安全的冷冻舱里。"
她微微耸了耸肩。
"结果发现，他建造了超空间分流器，建造了伊甸园，发起了一场宗教革命，通过星门消失，并在一个大小如同一整个太阳系的世界里独自度过了余生。"
她停顿了一下。
"所以我稍微调整了一下自己的预期。"
entries.backTranslation:
Isaac let out a breath.
" Is it bad? Is it strange? "
She turned the tablet over and over in her hands.
" I’ve spent most of my life wondering if Isaac Lester is my father. I guess he might have been an astronaut. If I’m lucky, maybe he was an engineer. Or perhaps he was someone trapped in the collapse who stuffed his child into the safest cryogenic chamber he could find. "
She shrugged slightly.
"It turns out he built the hyperspace diverter, created Eden, sparked a religious revolution, vanished through the Stargate, and spent the rest of his life alone on a world the size of an entire solar system. "
She paused for a moment.
" So I adjusted my expectations slightly. "

entries.source:
The workshop is silent.
Isa's entire team has gathered beneath the Onslaught Mk.I's projected silhouette. Salvagers who normally argue over stripped bolts stand shoulder to shoulder with yard engineers, all staring upward. The shape is crude and strangely proportioned, but unmistakable.
Isa does not look away when you enter.
"Do you understand what you brought home?" she asks quietly. "The Onslaught. The one every other has spent thousands of cycles trying to remember."
entries.target:
车间里一片寂静。
艾萨的整个团队都聚集在攻势 Mk.I号投影出的剪影下方。那些平时总为拆下的螺栓争执不休的回收者，此刻正与船坞工程师们并肩而立，所有人都在仰头凝视。那个轮廓虽然粗糙且比例怪异，却毫无疑问就是它。
你走进来时，艾萨的目光并未移开。
"你明白自己带回了什么吗？"她轻声问道。 "攻势号。那艘让其他人耗费了数千个周期仍试图回忆的飞船。"

"Enough." The reverence in Isa's voice gives way to mounting professional excitement. She unfolds diagrams of the replaceable vambrace armor, the shieldless hull, and the electromechanical automation whispering through every major system.
"The crew kept rebuilding themselves alongside it. Wounded, augmented, replaced, until the people and the ship stopped being separate things. All that remained was a factory serial and one final order repeated across the ages."
A fire-control pattern detaches from the diagrams. You recall what the ship said when you were there.

entries.source:
For once, Isa has no slate in her hands. No schematics, no lists, no half-disassembled parts balanced on the furniture. Just a travel case at her feet and a hard little smile she is trying, unsuccessfully, to hide.
"The Hall can run without me staring over its shoulder now," she says. "Every ledger is clean. Every weird old hull has taught us what it was going to teach from a dock. So if you'll have me, Captain, I want to join you. I want to see what legacies looks like when they're being made."
entries.target:
难得一见，艾萨手中没有石板。没有图纸，没有清单，也没有半拆解的零件平衡在家具上。 脚边只有一个旅行箱，还有那抹她试图掩饰却未能成功的小小冷笑。
"现在‘凯旋大厅'已经不需要我时刻在旁边监督了，"她说道。 "每本账簿都清清楚楚。每一艘古怪的老船体，都已在码头边教会了我们它所能传授的一切。所以，船长，如果您愿意接纳我，我想加入您的队伍。 我想亲眼见证遗产在缔造时的模样。"
entries.backTranslation:
It was a rare sight—Isa wasn’t holding a slate. There were no blueprints, no checklists, and no partially disassembled parts balanced on the furniture. At her feet lay only a suitcase, along with that faint, cold smile she tried—but failed—to hide.
" The ‘Hall of Triumph’ no longer needs me to supervise it constantly, " she said. " Every ledger is in perfect order. Every one of those strange old hulls has taught us everything it could at the dock. So, Captain, if you’re willing to take me on, I’d like to join your crew. I want to witness with my own eyes what a legacy looks like as it’s being forged. "

She sticks out a daintier hand than you were expecting.

Isa does an exaggerated curtsy.
"Ma'am!" she repeats. "Hear that?" She calls over her shoulder, to the genial cheers of her men. "We're respectable citizens now!"
Isa straightens and gives your entourage an appraising look. Her gaze passes over the uniforms, the sidearms, and finally the power-armored marines at your back. You swear you can see her smile widen.

"And on you, $shipTrophyIsaBarPlayerRank. May your reactors run cool, your seals hold pressure, and every unexploded missile stay that way until someone else finds it. Aaaaa-Men."
She smiles.
"Every spacer finds religion eventually. Usually right after the life-support alarms start."

" Every astronaut eventually turns to religion. Usually after the life support system alarm goes off. "

"Well, I'll cut to the chase, $shipTrophyIsaBarPlayerRank." Isa looks up. "I saw your vanity project out there. Your 'Hall of Triumph'. All those amazing ships with hundreds of cycles of history... I want you to hire us to research those ship frames."
Isa looks out to the window wall that makes up the bar. For the first time, her eyes steady and her gaze turns far away. Another ship is floating in from dock, being towed into your museum. "It really is incredible..."
entries.target:
"好吧，我长话短说，$shipTrophyIsaBarPlayerRank。" 艾萨抬头望去。"我看到外面那个你自娱自乐的项目了。 你的凯旋殿堂。那些承载着数百个周期历史的惊人飞船……我想让你雇佣我们来研究那些船体框架。"
艾萨望向构成酒吧的落地窗墙。 这是她第一次眼神变得坚定，目光投向远方。又一艘飞船正从码头漂浮而来，被拖曳进你的博物馆。"这真的太不可思议了……"
entries.backTranslation:
" Alright, I’ll make this quick, $shipTrophyIsaBarPlayerRank. " Isa looked up. " I saw that little side project of yours out there. Your Hall of Triumph. Those astonishing spacecraft that carry hundreds of cycles of history… I’d like you to hire us to study those hull frames. "
Isa looked toward the floor-to-ceiling glass wall that made up the bar. For the first time, her gaze grew determined as she looked into the distance. Another spaceship was drifting in from the dock, being towed into your museum. " This is truly incredible… "

entries.source:
A private channel opens on the fleet's command display. Isa is standing only a few steps away, but she has routed a live gallery feed from $shipTrophyIsaCompletionHomeName across the screen before saying anything.
The view settles on ranks of restored hulls beneath the gallery lights, each faction's doctrine preserved in steel, circuitry, and old scars.
"I wanted to see it from out here," Isa says at last. "The whole thing at once. One last time, before I leave."
"You've done it, Captain. The Hall of Triumph is done. Not finished, mind you; places like this are never finished. But every core ledger is preserved under one roof. Not under war, but peace."
Isa glances from the distant gallery to the fleet around you. "The Hall can preserve what came before. From here on, we get to make what comes next. Thank you for giving me a place in it."
entries.target:
舰队指挥显示屏上弹出一个私人频道。艾萨就站在几步之外，但在开口说话前，她已将来自$shipTrophyIsaCompletionHomeName的实时展厅画面投射到屏幕上。
画面定格在观景台灯光下的修复船体行列上，各阵营的作战理念都铭刻在钢铁、电路和旧伤痕之中。
"我想从这里看一眼，"艾萨终于开口道。"把这一切尽收眼底。 在我离开之前，最后一次。"
"您做到了，舰长。凯旋殿堂已经建成。不过请注意，这并非完工；像这样的地方永远不会完工。 但每一本核心账簿都已安然保存于同一屋檐下。不是在战火之中，而是在和平之中。"
艾萨的目光从远处的观景廊掠向你周围的舰队。"这座大厅能够保存过往的一切。 从今往后，我们将共同开创未来。感谢您让我在其中占有一席之地。"
entries.backTranslation:
A private channel popped up on the fleet command display. Isa was standing just a few steps away, but before she spoke, she had already projected the real-time exhibition hall feed from $shipTrophyIsaCompletionHomeName onto the screen. The
feed was frozen on a row of hulls under repair, illuminated by the observation deck’s lights; the combat philosophies of each faction were etched into the steel, circuitry, and old battle scars.
" I’d like to take a look from here, " Isa finally said. " To take it all in. One last time, before I leave. "
" You've done it, Captain. The Hall of Triumph is complete. But please note, this is not the end; a place like this is never truly finished. But every Core Ledger has been safely preserved under one roof—not amidst the flames of war, but in peace. "
Isa’s gaze swept from the distant observation gallery to the fleet surrounding you. " This hall preserves all of our past. From this day forward, we will forge the future together. Thank you for allowing me to have a place within it. "

entries.source:
Shattered Ring comes into view one broken section at a time.
Three vast arcs circle the barren moon below, each turning at a slightly different rate. Pressurized bridges, cargo gantries, and naked lengths of structural cable span some of the gaps. Others remain open to space, their severed ends capped with bulkheads scavenged from old ships.
The self-governing colony looks less constructed than prevented from falling apart. Isa appears beside the navigation station and plants both hands on your navigator’s desk.
"Take us around the dark side."
Your navigator glances at the approach plot.
"Traffic beacon’s directing us sunward."
"That traffic beacon’s been wrong since I was twelve."
entries.target:
破碎之环正以断裂的片段为单位逐渐映入眼帘。
三道巨大的弧线环绕着下方的荒芜卫星，每道旋转的速度略有不同。加压桥、货运龙门架以及裸露的结构缆索横跨部分间隙。 其余部分则直接暴露在太空中，断裂的末端用从旧船上回收的舱壁封堵着。
这座自治殖民地看起来与其说是经过建造，不如说是勉强维持着不至于分崩离析。 艾萨出现在导航站旁，双手撑在你的导航员桌面上。
"带我们绕行至暗面。"
你的导航员瞥了一眼进近图。
"交通信标正引导我们朝太阳方向飞去。"
"那个交通信标从我十二岁起就一直出错。"
entries.backTranslation:
The Shattered Ring is gradually coming into view, piece by piece.
Three massive arcs encircle the barren moon below, each rotating at a slightly different speed. Pressurized bridges, cargo gantries, and exposed structural cables span some of the gaps. The remaining sections are directly exposed to space, their fractured ends sealed with bulkheads salvaged from old ships.
This autonomous colony seems less like a constructed structure and more like one that’s barely being held together to prevent it from falling apart. Isa appears beside the navigation station, resting her hands on your navigator’s desk.
" Take us around to the dark side. "
Your navigator glances at the approach chart.
" The traffic beacon is guiding us toward the sun. "
" That traffic beacon has been malfunctioning ever since I was twelve. "

As if summoned by the insult, the comm channel crackles.
"Approaching fleet, inbound bearing zero-three-five, elevation minus one-two. Reduce velocity and prepare to receive docking procedures—"
Isa leans over the console.
"Arthur? Tell Garret it’s me."
There is a long pause.
"Isaac?" another voice says. "Thought we were finally rid of you."
"Call me that again and I’ll come up there and kick your butt all over comms."
Garret laughs.
"Roger that. Take the locals' approach queue. You know the way. Over."
Isa closes the channel.
"Bay Fourteen," she tells the navigator, pointing at a row of glowing beacons hidden behind one of the arcs.
entries.target:
仿佛是被这句侮辱召唤了一般，通讯频道传来噼啪声。
" 舰队正在接近，入场方位零-三-五，仰角负一-二。 降低航速并准备接收对接指令——"
艾萨俯身在控制台前。
"亚瑟？告诉加雷特是我。"
随后是一段漫长的沉默。
" 艾萨克？" 另一个声音说道。 "我还以为我们终于摆脱你了呢。"
"你再这么叫我，我就冲上去，在通讯频道里把你揍得满地找牙。"
加勒特笑了起来。
"收到。 走当地人的进近航线。你知道路。完毕。"
艾萨关闭了通信频道。
"十四号航道，"她对导航员说道，同时指着隐藏在其中一个弧形结构后方的一排发光信标。
entries.backTranslation:
As if summoned by this insult, a crackling sound came over the communication channel.
" The fleet is approaching, entry bearing zero-three-five, elevation negative one-two. Reduce speed and prepare to receive docking instructions—"

A long silence followed.
" Isaac? " another voice said. " I thought we’d finally gotten rid of you. "
" If you call me that one more time, I’ll come at you and beat the crap out of you right here on the comm channel. "
Garrett laughed.
" Copy that. Take the local approach route. You know the way. Over. "
Isa closed the communication channel.
" Runway 14, " she said to the navigator, pointing to a row of glowing beacons hidden behind one of the curved structures.

Bay Fourteen accepts your approaching fleet with a tremendous metallic cacophony.
The entire docking tube shudders as the clamps engage. Something heavy strikes the outer hull, tumbles away, and disappears beneath the berth.
Isa waits for the noise to stop.
"Perfect."
Everyone on your bridge exchanges looks. The docking tube groans again. Your flagship shifts in its berth with a tremendous crunch.
"Even more perfect."
entries.target:
十四号泊位伴随着震耳欲聋的金属撞击声迎接你驶近的舰队。
当夹具锁定时，整个对接管都剧烈震颤。有重物撞击外层船体，翻滚着飞开，随后消失在泊位下方。
艾萨等待着噪音平息。
"完美。"
指挥桥上的所有人互相对视。 对接管再次发出呻吟。你的旗舰在泊位中剧烈晃动，伴随着巨大的嘎吱声。
"简直完美。"
entries.backTranslation:
Dock 14 greets your approaching fleet with a deafening clang of metal.
As the docking clamps lock into place, the entire docking tube shakes violently. A heavy object strikes the outer hull, tumbles away, and then vanishes beneath the berth.
Isa waits for the noise to subside.
" Perfect. "
Everyone on the command bridge exchanged glances. The docking tube groaned again. Your flagship shook violently in its berth, accompanied by a loud creaking sound.
" Absolutely perfect. "

entries.source:
By the time you reach the main concourse, word has spread.
Dockworkers call to Isa from the overhead gantries. A food vendor reaches across his counter to press a foil-wrapped pastry into her hand. Someone shouts that the recycler on Level Six is making the drinking water taste metallic again.
A child in an oversized pressure suit runs up and presents her with a cracked maneuvering thruster valve. Isa crouches, turns it over in her hands, and tells him which seal needs replacing.
Before you have crossed half the concourse, one of your bodyguards is carrying a crate of machine parts for an elderly mechanic. Another is holding a ladder steady while Isa points out a flickering light panel for an electrician.
Nobody has asked who you are.
entries.target:
等你抵达主大厅时，消息已经传开了。
码头工人从头顶的龙门架上向艾萨喊话。一位食品摊贩越过柜台，将一个铝箔包裹的糕点塞进她的手里。 有人高喊，六层的回收装置又让饮用水带上了金属味。
一个身穿宽松压力服的孩子跑过来，递给她一个裂开的机动推进器阀门。 艾萨蹲下身，在手中翻转着那个阀门，告诉他需要更换哪个密封圈。
还没走过中庭一半的距离，你的保镖之一就已经正为一位年迈的机械师搬运一箱机器零件。 另一名保镖正稳稳地扶着梯子，而艾萨则指着一块闪烁的照明面板向电工说明情况。
没有人问过你是谁。
entries.backTranslation:
By the time you reached the main hall, the news had already spread.
Dockworkers shouted down to Isa from the gantry overhead. A food vendor leaned over the counter and shoved a foil-wrapped pastry into her hand. Someone shouted that the recycling unit on Level 6 had once again given the drinking water a metallic taste.
A child in a baggy pressure suit ran over and handed her a cracked jetpack valve. Isa squatted down, turning the valve over in her hand, and told him which O-ring needed to be replaced.
Before she had even crossed halfway through the atrium, one of your bodyguards was already helping an elderly mechanic carry a crate of machine parts. Another bodyguard is holding a ladder steady, while Isa points to a flickering light panel and explains the situation to an electrician.
No one has asked who you are.

An old salvage foreman is waiting when Isa climbs down.
He wears a patched station utility suit, its original insignia hidden beneath decades of repairs. Under one arm, he carries a narrow metal case marked with faded cryogenic-handling symbols.
Isa’s good humor disappears.
"Where did you get that?"
"Found it behind the plating in Calder’s old storeroom," the foreman says. "Station council was clearing out abandoned property."
He holds the case toward her.
The people passing through the concourse give the three of you a wide berth. Finally, Isa wipes her hands against her trousers and accepts the case.
"Thanks."

entries.backTranslation:
As Isa climbed down, an elderly salvage foreman was waiting.
He wore a space station jumpsuit patched beyond recognition, its original insignia obscured by decades of mending. Tucked under his arm was a narrow, elongated metal box bearing a faded cryogenic symbol.
Isa’s good mood vanished instantly.
" Where did this thing come from? "
" It was found behind some sheet metal in the old storage room at Calder, " the foreman said. " The station committee is clearing out abandoned items. "
He handed the box to her.
People passing through the lobby were making a wide berth around the three of you. Finally, Isa wiped her hands on her pants and took the box.
" Thank you. "

entries.source:
Isa leads you through the station without speaking.
You descend through Arc Two, past hydroponics bays and crowded habitation decks, until the finished corridors give way to exposed conduits and old pressure doors.
The gravity weakens with each level.
Isa adjusts automatically, shortening her steps whenever the deck shifts beneath her. Your bodyguards are less graceful. One catches the overhead piping to avoid drifting into a wall.
At last, Isa opens an abandoned machine shop.
Several names have been carved into the pressure door. Hers is among them, scratched low enough that whoever wrote it must have been very young.
ISA LESESTER IS DA BEST.
entries.target:

重力随着每层楼的下降而减弱。
艾萨会自动调整步伐，每当脚下的甲板发生位移时，她便会缩短步幅。你的保镖们就没那么优雅了。 其中一人抓住了头顶的管道，以免被漂移撞上墙壁。
终于，艾萨打开了一间废弃的机械车间。
压力门上刻着几个名字。 她的名字也在其中，刻得位置很低，看来刻下这个名字的人当时一定还很年轻。
ISA LEICESTER SHI ZUI BANG DE!

"My great claim to fame," Isa says, smiling. "Youngest ‘pod person’ on my Arc."
A small metal contact is visible beneath the scorched collar.
Isa stops smiling.
"That wasn’t there before."
She releases the preservation seal and carefully lifts the suit onto the workbench. The fabric crackles as she turns the collar over, shedding small flecks of decayed plastic onto the surface below.
The frayed insulation has exposed an identification wafer embedded beneath the name strip.
Isa removes her slate.
On scan, her slate’s display splits into dozens of windows. Her delta-level AI agents begin testing ancient authentication protocols, interpolating damaged sectors, and comparing the wafer against surviving Domain registries.
"You don’t have to stay," she says.

entries.source:
Isa returns to the slate.
Her agents scatter through the surviving Domain archives, following Isaac Leicester’s registry number through personnel rosters, departmental accounts, procurement records, and damaged transit indexes.
Most references vanish as soon as they begin to resolve.
DCR-2F38-CB017-6A
The number appears beside a Heliostructural Systems roster.
Then a classified procurement authorization.
Then a personnel-transfer order whose destination disappears beneath another INFOSEC warning.
Isa opens the failed queries side by side.
"What are you doing?" you ask.
"Looking at how they break."

大多数线索刚一浮现便随即消失。
DCR-2F38-CB017-6A
该编号出现在日构系统公司的名册旁。
接着是一份机密采购授权书。
随后是一份人员调动令，其目的地被另一条INFOSEC警告所遮蔽。
艾萨将这些未成功的查询并排打开。

"在看它们是怎么出错的。"

A damaged manifest opens above the workbench.
PENELOPE’S STAR GATE TRANSIT AUTHORITY
OUTBOUND PASSENGER CONTROL
Most of the record is unreadable. Names and registry numbers emerge briefly between broken columns and access warnings.
One line illuminates.
GATE OUTBOUND TRANSIT AUTHORIZATION
PASSENGER: INFOSEC RESTRICTED
CITIZEN REGISTRY: INFOSEC RESTRICTED
ORIGIN: PENELOPE’S STAR
DECLARED DESTINATION: SOL
TRANSIT STATUS: AUTHORIZED
Isa places the manifest beside Isaac’s citizen record.
Both restricted fields fail in precisely the same way.
She watches the paired distortions repeat.
Then she says:
"That’s him."

For a while, she says nothing. The old suit remains spread across the workbench between you, Isaac Leicester’s name blackened but still legible beneath the collar. Then she closes the file.
"Captain."
Her voice has lost its earlier lightness.
"I know this isn’t fleet business. But somebody went to a lot of trouble to hide whatever he was building. I don’t think I’m going to get much further by myself."
Isa looks directly at you.
"I want to find out who Isaac Leicester was. What happened to him. How his suit ended up wrapped around me."
She hesitates.
"I’m also asking for your help."

"船长。"

"我知道这不关舰队的事。 但有人费了很大劲去隐藏他正在制造的东西。我觉得靠我一个人恐怕很难再有进展。"

"我想查明艾萨克·莱斯特究竟是谁。他遭遇了什么。他的飞行服又是怎么裹在我身上的。"
她犹豫了一下。
"我也需要你的帮助。"
entries.backTranslation:
She was silent for a moment. That old uniform was still spread out on the control console between you; though the name Isaac Lester below the collar had faded and turned black, it was still legible. Then she closed the file folder.
" Captain. "
Her voice no longer had its previous lightness.
" I know this isn’t the Fleet’s business. But someone went to great lengths to hide what he was building. I’m afraid I won’t be able to make any further progress on my own. "
Isa looked straight at you.
" I want to find out exactly who Isaac Lester is. What happened to him. And how did his flight suit end up wrapped around me? "
She hesitated for a moment.
" I need your help, too. "

Cherubim and Lahat Haharev pivot in exact counterpoint. No hail follows. No warning asks you to keep your distance.
Your own identification packet returns instead, stripped of its header and divided into two mirrored copies.

entries.source:
The second hypershunt is already under attack.
Pather demolition ships cling to one of the collector spines. Shaped charges crawl across the black superstructure in glittering chains while scripture floods every open frequency: condemnation of the machine and promises of cleansing fire.
Across the structure, pirate cutting rigs have anchored directly to the transmission vanes. Industrial lasers bite into armor thick enough to roof cities. Salvage tugs wait behind them with their holds open, ready to carry off whatever the crews can tear loose before the Pathers bring the whole structure down.
The two flotillas fire past one another, each too committed to its work to disengage.
Isa sees the charge telemetry.
"No."
She enlarges the carrier spine, watching warning glyphs multiply across the projection.
"This is the only clue we have left. If they destroy that spine, Isaac's record goes with it."
The first Pather charge arms. A pirate tug wrenches a glowing section of armor away from the hypershunt.
The ship carrying Isa rolls out of formation before you can answer.
"Helm, bring us in. All batteries, engage. Get them away from my hypershunt."
entries.target:
第二条超空间通道已遭到袭击。
帕瑟号爆破舰正紧贴着其中一根收集脊。 成串的成形炸药如闪烁的链条般在漆黑的上层结构上蔓延，与此同时，经文淹没了所有开放频率：既有对机器的谴责，也有关于净化之火的承诺。
在整个结构上，海盗切割装置已直接锚定在传动叶片上。工业激光正啃噬着足以覆盖整座城市的厚重装甲。 打捞拖船在后方敞开货舱待命，准备在帕瑟号将整座结构体摧毁之前，运走船员们能撕扯下来的任何残骸。
两支舰队互相交火，各自都因过于专注于自己的任务而无法脱离交战。
艾萨看到了装药的遥测数据。
"不。"
她放大航母主梁的投影，看着警告符号在投影上不断增多。
"这是我们仅剩的线索。如果他们摧毁了那条主干，艾萨克的记录也将随之消失。"
第一枚帕瑟炸弹已装填完毕。一艘海盗拖船将超空间分流器上发光的一段装甲强行扯了下来。
在你来得及回应之前，载有艾萨的飞船便脱离了编队。
"舵手，将我们开过去。所有炮台，开火。把他们从我的超空间分流器旁赶走。"

entries.source:
You lower your voice.
"The machine is not the object of our pilgrimage. We seek only what the servants of Moloch tried to bury within it."
You speak of false wonders, poisoned knowledge, and the duty of the faithful to expose the sins of the old Domain without claiming its power for themselves.
The commander studies you for a long moment.
At last, he nods.
"Then go, brother. For the Prophet’s sake, go."
The Pather fleet begins clearing the approach corridor.
entries.target:
你压低了声音。
"这台机器并非我们朝圣的目的。 我们只寻求摩洛克的仆从试图将其深埋其中的东西。"
你所说的，是虚假的奇观、被毒化的知识，以及信徒的职责——揭露旧人之领的罪孽，却不为自己夺取其力量。
指挥官凝视着你良久。
最后，他点了点头。
"那么去吧，兄弟。 为了先知的缘故，去吧。"
帕瑟舰队开始清理进近通道。
entries.backTranslation:
You lowered your voice.
" This machine is not the purpose of our pilgrimage. We seek only what Moloch’s minions attempted to bury deep within it. "
What you speak of is false spectacle, poisoned knowledge, and the duty of the faithful—to expose the sins of the Old Ones’ domain, yet not to seize their power for oneself.
The commander gazed at you for a long time.
Finally, he nodded.
" Then go, brother. For the sake of the Prophet, go. "
The Passer Fleet begins clearing the approach corridor.

entries.source:
With the approach corridor clear, your fleet closes on the hypershunt.
The structure grows across the forward display until it no longer resembles a machine. Black towers rise through the stellar corona, joined by collector vanes and transmission spines large enough to eclipse cities. Streams of plasma bend around it in slow, incandescent arches.
Isa stands beside the sensor station, slate in hand.
"We’ll need to map the whole thing."
She begins assigning survey patterns across the fleet.
"Field geometry. Collector alignment. Residual phase harmonics. Anything the Domain tuned by hand."
entries.target:
随着进近航道畅通，你的舰队正逼近超空间分流器。
该结构在前方显示屏上逐渐放大，直至不再像一台机器。黑色高塔从恒星日冕中拔地而起，与收集叶片和传输脊柱相连，其规模之大足以遮蔽整座城市。 等离子流在它周围弯曲，形成缓慢而炽热的光弧。
艾萨站在传感器站旁，手中拿着石板。
"我们需要绘制整个结构的地图。"
她开始向整个舰队分配勘测方案。
"场几何结构。收集器对齐。 残余相位谐波。任何由人之领手工调校过的部分。"
entries.backTranslation:
With the approach route clear, your fleet is closing in on the hyperspace diverter.
The structure gradually enlarges on the forward display until it no longer resembles a machine. Plasma streams curve around it, forming slow, incandescent arcs of light.
Isa stands beside the sensor station, a tablet in her hand.
" We need to map the entire structure. "
She began assigning survey plans to the entire fleet.
" Field geometry. Collector alignment. Residual phase harmonics. Any components manually fine-tuned by human hands. "

Sensor craft trace the curvature of its containment fields. Gravimetric probes measure distortions along the transmission spines. Isa’s agents compare the results against surviving Domain engineering standards and the concealed routing data recovered at Shattered Ring.
Most of the structure follows standard automated tolerances.
Several sections do not.

Tiny deviations recur across the hypershunt’s oldest assemblies: corrections too consistent to be random, repeated through construction phases separated by centuries.
Isa overlays them.
A familiar authorization pattern emerges from the accumulated calibration data.
DCR-2F38-CB017-6A
LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
CONTINUITY AUTHORITY
Isa leans closer.
"That’s him."
The same pattern appears in the hypershunt’s transmission geometry, attached to a routing vector concealed beneath SUPER ALABASTER restriction.
[A sealed personal log is embedded beside the routing data.]

entries.source:
The recording terminates abruptly.
Isa does not move.
The hypershunt burns across the forward display behind her, its black superstructure suspended within the stellar corona.
After a long silence, she looks down at the microchip connected to her slate.
"His daughter."
She swallows.
"They were supposed to wake her together."
Her eyes move back over the revival report.
"Rebecca died, and he never opened the other pod."
entries.target:
录音戛然而止。
艾萨一动不动。
超空间分流在她的身后穿过前置显示屏，其黑色上层结构悬浮于恒星日冕之中。
经过漫长的沉默，她低头看着连接在平板上的微芯片。
"他的女儿。"
她咽了口唾沫。
"他们本该一起唤醒她的。"
她的目光又移回复苏报告上。
"丽贝卡死了，而他从未打开过另一个茧舱。"
entries.backTranslation:

" They were supposed to wake her up together. "

" Rebecca was dead, and he had never opened the other pod. "

entries.source:
The carrier signal continues repeating beneath the silence.
Isa scrolls back through the recovered fragments, reading the same lines again.
"He never named her."
"I know," she says before you can answer.
Isa grips the edge of her slate.
"The suit. His identification. This log, somehow encoded within the Hypershunt. All of it was meant to be a message to... to me."
She shakes her head.
"But my pod was opened centuries after this was recorded. I don’t know what happened between."
She stares at the carrier trace.
"Or was he trying to come back?"
entries.target:
在寂静之下，载波信号仍在不断重复。
艾萨向后翻阅恢复的碎片，再次读着相同的行文。
"他从未给过她名字。"
"我知道，"她在你来得及回答之前说道。
艾萨紧握着石板的边缘。
"那套制服。他的身份证明。这本日志，不知怎么被编码进了超空间跳跃器里。这一切本意都是要向……向我传达的信息。"
她摇了摇头。
"但我的舱室是在这段记录完成几个世纪后才被打开的。我不知道这期间发生了什么。"
她凝视着载波轨迹。
"还是说，他当时正试图回来？"
entries.backTranslation:
Beneath the silence, the carrier signal continued to repeat.
Isa flipped back through the recovered fragments, reading the same lines again.
" He had never given her a name. "
" I know, " she said before you could answer.
Isa gripped the edge of the stone tablet tightly.
" That uniform. His ID. This log—somehow encoded into the hyperspace jumper. All of this was meant to be a message for… for me. "
She shook her head.
" But my pod wasn’t opened until centuries after this recording was made. I don’t know what happened during that time. "
She stared at the carrier’s trajectory.
" Or was he trying to come back at that time? "

The recording ends.
Isa remains fixed on the last line.
Nothing changed.
The hypershunt’s signal begins repeating beneath it, carrying the words back into the stellar corona.
Isa stops the playback.
"He forgot her face."
She says it quietly.
"Rebecca's. My mother's."
Her fingers remain poised above the slate.
[Recovered Log — Part III.]

entries.source:
The Power Transit Gate closes behind your fleet.
For several seconds, nobody on the bridge says anything. The first thing you hear are altitude warnings. Your navigation display struggles to decide which way is down. Gravitational calibration spins like a top.
Then through the CIC's viewcams, you see it.
Gan Eden rises below you. Closes in above you. Rises all around you.
entries.target:
动力中转星门在你的舰队身后关闭。
几秒钟内，指挥桥上无人发声。你听到的第一声是高度警告。导航显示屏正竭力判断哪个方向是下方。 重力校准系统像陀螺一样飞速旋转。
随后，通过作战指挥中心的监控摄像头，你看到了它。
伊甸园在你下方升起，在你上方逼近，在你四周升腾。
entries.backTranslation:
The energy portal closes behind your fleet.
For several seconds, no one on the command bridge speaks. The first sound you hear is a high-altitude warning. The navigation display is struggling to determine which direction is down. The gravity calibration system spins rapidly like a gyroscope.
Then, through the surveillance cameras in the operations center, you saw it.
Ganiden rose beneath you, closed in above you, and swirled all around you.

entries.source:
Oceans stretch across the inner surface of the world, blue expanses thousands of kilometers wide. Mountain chains climb toward the horizon until distance turns them pale, then continue overhead. Cloud systems drift across continents suspended impossibly above you, their shadows moving over forests and inland seas.
There is no horizon in any direction. Only a solar-system sized, singular world.
There are no words to say. You see several of your bridge members reach out to hug each other.
Then every alarm on Isa's slate goes off at once.
entries.target:
海洋铺展在世界的内表面，宽达数千公里的蓝色广袤。山脉向地平线蜿蜒延伸，直至因距离而变得苍白，随后继续向头顶延伸。云系漂浮在大陆上方——这些大陆悬浮在你头顶，仿佛违背常理——它们的阴影在森林和内陆海之上移动。
无论朝哪个方向，都看不到地平线。 只有一个太阳系大小的、独一无二的世界。
无言以表。你看到几名桥上成员伸出手互相拥抱。
随后，艾萨平板上的所有警报同时响起。
entries.backTranslation:
The ocean stretches across the world’s inner surface, a vast expanse of blue thousands of kilometers wide. Mountain ranges wind toward the horizon until they fade to a pale hue due to the distance, then continue to rise overhead. Cloud formations drift above the continents—which hover overhead, seemingly defying the laws of nature—their shadows shifting across the forests and inland seas.
No matter which direction you look, there is no horizon in sight. Only a single, unique world the size of a solar system.
Words fail you. You see several members of the Bridge reach out to embrace one another.
Then, all the alarms on Isa’s console sound simultaneously.

"Gravitational reference error. Local vertical unresolved." Isa mutters, barely able to tear her eyes away. "Atmosphere where atmosphere shouldn't be—"  Isa mutters, barely able to tear her eyes away from the scenery.
She kills the warnings one after another.
Another window opens.
Isa stops.
She stares at it long enough that you turn from the viewport.
"...wait."
Her fingers move across the slate.
A thin signal resolves out of the noise.

艾萨停下了脚步。

entries.backTranslation:
" Gravity reference error. Local vertical coordinates not determined. " Isa muttered, barely able to tear his gaze away from what lay before him. " An atmosphere had appeared where there shouldn’t have been one—" Isa muttered, barely able to tear her gaze away from the scene before her.
She closed the warnings one after another.
Another window popped up.
Isa stopped in her tracks.
She stared at the window for a long time—so long that you had to look away from the viewing port.
"… Wait a minute. "
Her fingers glided across the stone slab.
A faint signal emerged from the static.

entries.source:
"Active distress beacon," she says.
There is sudden excitement in her voice. Then she reads the header.
She looks back at the impossible world surrounding your fleet.
The signal repeats.
Isa opens the attached navigation packet.
"Source is planetside. Or... shell-side. Whatever we're calling it."
Your ship's AI spends several seconds inventing a coordinate system capable of describing the destination.
Then a name appears.
TREE OF LIFE
EDEN PRIMARY BIOSPHERE
EMERGENCY ACCESS
entries.target:

她的声音中突然透出兴奋。 随后她读出了报头。

" The signal source was located on the surface of a planet. Or… the surface of a shell. Whatever we choose to call it. "

A name then appeared.

entries.source:
Your fleet touches down beneath the Tree of Life.
For a while, nobody seems to know what to do.
The landing grounds lie beneath a vast canopy of living green, the trunks rising between grey, uniform towers and terraces until the branches close together overhead like the roof of a cathedral. Warm air moves through the open ramps carrying the smell of soil, leaves, and water.
Requests for shore leave begin almost immediately.
By the time the first reports reach you, entire deck crews are offering detailed explanations for why their particular ship can absolutely spare them for an hour.
Your captains recommend a compromise: short rotating leave. The schedule is approved with suspicious enthusiasm.
When the first rotation comes down the ramps, some of the spacers simply stop.
entries.target:
你的舰队在生命之树下着陆。
有一段时间，似乎没人知道该做什么。
着陆场位于一片广阔的鲜活绿荫之下，树干从灰色的、千篇一律的塔楼和露台之间拔地而起，枝桠在头顶交织成密，宛如大教堂的穹顶。 温暖的空气从敞开的坡道中流过，带着泥土、树叶和水的气味。
几乎立刻就有船员提出上岸休假的请求。
当第一批报告传到你手中时，整个甲板船员都在详细解释，为什么他们的船绝对可以抽出一小时让他们上岸。
船长们建议采取折衷方案：短期的轮休。 该安排以一种令人起疑的热情获得了批准。
当第一批轮休人员沿着坡道走下来时，有些太空人干脆停下了脚步。
entries.backTranslation:
Your fleet lands beneath the Tree of Life.
For a moment, no one seems to know what to do.
The landing pad lay beneath a vast expanse of vibrant greenery; tree trunks rose from the ground between the gray, monotonous towers and terraces, their branches weaving a dense canopy overhead, much like the dome of a cathedral. Warm air flowed through the open ramps, carrying the scent of earth, leaves, and water.
Almost immediately, crew members began requesting shore leave.
By the time the first reports reached you, the entire deck crew was explaining in detail why their ship could absolutely spare an hour to let them go ashore.
The captains suggested a compromise: short-term rotations. The arrangement was approved with suspicious enthusiasm.
As the first group of crew members on rotation walked down the ramp, some astronauts simply stopped in their tracks.

entries.source:
Most have seen nothing but hydroponics decks and cramped crew quarters their entire lives. Some have even visited abundant worlds like Gilead. The ones who have not walk out into the grass and lie down in it, staring up through the branches into the strange, inverted shell-sky.
Before long, the landing grounds are dotted with off-duty crew doing exactly the same thing. Some of them start a kickball match.
You make a mental note to have the watches keep careful count when each rotation returns. AWOL incidents would be epidemic. Isa stands at the foot of the ramp, staring upward.
For once, she seems to have forgotten the slate in her hand.
entries.target:
大多数人一辈子除了水培甲板和拥挤的船员宿舍外，别无所见。有些人甚至去过像 Gilead 那样物产丰饶的星球。那些没去过的人走上草地，躺在草丛中，透过树枝仰望那奇异的、倒置的贝壳状天空。
没过多久，停机坪上便零星散落着下班的船员，他们正做着完全一样的事。其中一些人开始了一场踢球比赛。
你暗自提醒自己，等每批轮班人员返回时，要让值班人员仔细清点人数。 擅离职守的事件恐怕会像瘟疫一样蔓延。艾萨站在坡道底部，抬头凝视着天空。
这一刻，她似乎暂时忘记了手中的石板。
entries.backTranslation:
Most people spend their entire lives seeing nothing but hydroponic decks and cramped crew quarters. Some have even visited bountiful planets like Gilead. Those who had never been there walked out onto the grass, lay down in the grass, and gazed up through the branches at that strange, upside-down, shell-shaped sky.
Before long, the apron was dotted with crew members off duty, doing exactly the same thing. Some of them started a game of soccer.
You silently reminded yourself that when each shift returned, you would have the duty officer carefully take roll call. Incidents of abandoning posts would likely spread like a plague. Isa stood at the bottom of the ramp, gazing up at the sky.
In that moment, she seemed to momentarily forget the slate in her hand.

entries.source:
The wind moves through the canopy far overhead. Sunlight breaks through in shifting columns, catching on leaves and the pale sides of the empty towers.
Wow. She mouths.
Her slate pings.
The moment is gone.
She looks down. Every sensor window has filled at once, the same signal that drew you to the Tree of Life is bleeding across channel after channel.
"That’s him."
entries.target:
风穿过头顶高处的树冠。阳光以变幻的柱状穿透云层，映照在树叶上，也映照在空荡塔楼那苍白的侧壁上。
哇。 她无声地念叨着。
她的石板发出叮的一声。
那一瞬间已然消逝。
她低头望去。 所有传感器窗口瞬间被填满，那个曾将你引向生命之树的信号，正不断蔓延至一个又一个频道。
"就是他。"
entries.backTranslation:
The wind swept through the treetops high above. Sunlight pierced the clouds in shifting columns, illuminating the leaves and the pale side walls of the empty tower.
Wow, she murmured silently.
Her slate emitted a tinkling sound.
That moment had already vanished.
She looked down. All the sensor windows were instantly filled; the signal that had once led you to the Tree of Life was spreading continuously across channel after channel.
" It’s him. "

entries.source:
The settlement known as the Tree of Life is cleaner than anything has a right to be.
There are no sweepers, no maintenance crews, no little machines trundling along the paths like you might see at Tritachyon. Dust simply does not seem to settle. Water leaves no trace on the pale walls or glass, and fallen leaves collect in neat lines along the edges of the walkways, as though the city itself knows where they belong.
At the larger intersections, broad basins of crystal-clear water descend into deep reservoirs placed in the middle of the streets. Your suit's scanners immediately flag it as drinkable—almost absurdly free of contaminants.
entries.target:
那座名为生命之树的定居点，干净得超乎常理。
这里没有清扫工，没有维护人员，也没有像你在速子科技那样在小径上缓缓行进的小机器。灰尘似乎根本不会沉积下来。 水在苍白的墙壁或玻璃上不留痕迹，落叶沿着人行道的边缘整齐地排列成行，仿佛这座城市本身就知道它们该归于何处。
在较大的十字路口，宽阔的水池中清澈见底的水流向街道中央深邃的水库。 你宇航服上的扫描仪立刻显示这是可饮用的水——其中几乎完全不含污染物，这简直令人难以置信。
entries.backTranslation:
The settlement known as the Tree of Life was unnaturally clean.
There were no janitors, no maintenance workers, and no small machines slowly making their way along the paths like the ones you’d see in Tritachyon. Dust simply never seemed to settle. Water leaves no trace on the pale walls or glass, and fallen leaves are neatly arranged in rows along the edges of the sidewalks, as if the city itself knew exactly where they belonged.
At larger intersections, crystal-clear water flows from wide basins toward deep reservoirs in the center of the streets. The scanner on your spacesuit immediately indicates that this water is potable—it contains almost no contaminants whatsoever, which is simply unbelievable.

entries.source:
One of your bodyguards plops herself onto a stone bench. The woman lets out a tremendous sigh of contentment. Isa runs two fingers along the back of it and looks at them.
Nothing.
"Self-cleaning surfaces." She studies the spotless stone. "I see no conduits. So it isn't electrostatic. Catalytic perhaps?"
Her slate pulses again, the signal still so strong that it bleeds across every other sensor channel. Isa follows it away from the broad civic terraces and deeper beneath the roots of the Tree of Life, into a quieter district where the buildings are smaller and the streets narrow into shaded footpaths.
The signal leads you to an old workshop.
The door opens without resistance.
entries.target:
你的保镖之一扑通一声坐在石凳上。那名女子发出了一声满足的叹息。 艾萨用两根手指沿着长椅背面滑动，然后盯着手指看。
什么都没有。
"自清洁表面。"她仔细端详着这块一尘不染的石头。 "我没看到任何导管。所以这不是静电作用。或许是催化作用？"
她的平板再次闪烁，信号依然如此强烈，以至于干扰到了其他所有传感器通道。 艾萨循着信号，离开宽阔的市政露台，深入生命之树的根系之下，进入一个更安静的区域——那里建筑更小，街道收窄成树荫下的步行道。
信号将你引向一间老旧的工坊。
门毫无阻力地打开了。
entries.backTranslation:
One of your bodyguards plopped down onto a stone bench. The woman let out a satisfied sigh. Isa ran two fingers along the back of the bench, then stared at her fingers.
Nothing.
" Self-cleaning surface. " She scrutinized the spotless stone. " I don’t see any conduits. So this isn’t static electricity. Perhaps it’s a catalytic reaction? "
Her tablet flickered again; the signal was still so strong that it was interfering with all other sensor channels. Following the signal, Aisa left the spacious municipal terrace and ventured deep beneath the roots of the Tree of Life, entering a quieter area—where the buildings were smaller and the streets narrowed into tree-shaded walkways.
The signal led you to an old workshop.
The door swung open without a hint of resistance.

entries.source:
Inside, Gan Eden’s perfection finally gives way to something unmistakably human. Tools cover the benches. Components have been dismantled and rebuilt by hand. A narrow cot has been pushed against one wall, and beside it sits a small table with a teapot still resting on top.
Isa lifts the lid.
The inside is bone dry, with a dark ring of residue clinging to the bottom.
She puts it down carefully.
"He lived here."
One wall has been covered in calculations. At first they look like ordinary power-transfer notes. Isa studies them for several seconds, then steps closer. Hypershunt output frequencies have been broken apart and recombined alongside communications theory, with tiny variations marked through the carrier harmonics.
entries.target:
室内，伊甸园的完美终于让位于某种毋庸置疑的人性痕迹。工作台上堆满了工具。组件已被手工拆解并重新组装。一张窄窄的行军床被推到墙边，旁边放着一张小桌，桌上还摆着一只茶壶。
艾萨掀开壶盖。
壶内干得像块骨头，底部附着一圈深色的残留物。
她小心地把它放回原处。
"他曾住在这里。"

entries.backTranslation:
Inside, Eden's perfection has finally given way to unmistakable traces of humanity. The workbench is piled high with tools. Components have been manually disassembled and reassembled. A narrow cot has been pushed against the wall, next to a small table on which sits a teapot.
Isa lifted the lid of the teapot.
The inside was as dry as a bone, with a ring of dark residue clinging to the bottom.
She carefully set it back in its place.
" He had once lived here. "
The entire wall was covered with mathematical formulas. At first glance, these appeared to be ordinary notes on energy transfer. Aisa studied them for a few seconds, then stepped closer. The output frequency of the hyperspace diverter had been broken down and reassembled using communication theory, with subtle fluctuations marked in the carrier harmonics.

entries.source:
The Space Elevator rises from the inner surface into the atmosphere above Gan Eden. Its upper terminus remains dark, but the structure itself is intact.
Your fleet begins a cautious approach.
Two strange Omega Shards emerge from the atmospheric glare. They cross the approach corridor without hailing, their overlapping drive fields building a wall of impossible vectors ahead of you.
Every attempt to advance turns into lateral acceleration. Dampers scream. Navigation gives ground before the fleet is thrown bodily into the elevator's outer superstructure.
The Shards hold until you retreat, then disappear back into the curve of the world.

The space elevator pierces the atmosphere above Eden from its inner surface. Its top remains shrouded in darkness, but the structure itself is intact.
Your fleet begins to approach cautiously.
Two eerie Omega Fragments emerge from the blinding glare of the atmosphere. Without transmitting any communication signals, they cut across the approach corridor, their overlapping propulsion fields forming a barrier of impossible vectors directly ahead of you.
Every attempt to move forward is converted into lateral acceleration. The dampers emit a piercing screech. Navigation fails, and the fleet slams violently into the outer superstructure of the elevator.
These fragments remained in place until you retreated, then vanished into the curvature of the world.

With Cherubim and Lahat Ha-Cherev gone, the elevator's interdiction field is silent.
Isa's inherited suit transponder opens the outer doors.
The landing dock beyond is empty except for the wreck of a Kite shuttle, driven hard against one side of the platform. Its entire right wing was scorched away and much of the hull has been melted into slag by some enormous burst of energy. You have a fairly good idea which of the two constructs was responsible.
A dark trail begins beside the shattered cockpit. Nearly two centuries have reduced it to little more than a stain against the deck, but it continues away from the wreck and into the elevator, uneven and unmistakable.
Something dragged itself from the shuttle.
Your bodyguards and Isa follow the trail through the silent corridors toward the master control room. It ends in the hallway outside.
That is where Isaac Thomas Leicester is.
His remains lie against the wall, still sealed inside a vacuum suit. The helmet is cracked across the visor, and there is nothing visible within except darkness. An identification transponder on his back continues to pulse after all these years.
LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS.
Beside him lies a recording unit.
Isa sucks in a breath and drops to her knees beside the suit. Tears are already running down her face by the time she reaches toward him, stopping just short of touching the cracked helmet.
"The last log."
LOG — FINAL

entries.source:
RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART I
My name is Isaac Thomas Leicester, Director of Engineering for Heliostructural Systems in the Persean Sector.
My work included the construction of the coronal hypershunts and, later, Project Eden.
The projects were expected to take centuries. Eden might have required more than a thousand years before reaching its final design capacity. No ordinary succession of administrators could preserve the technical knowledge, institutional memory, and design intent required over such a span.
The Domain therefore established a continuity office. Its directors would serve across generations, entering cryosuspension between major phases of construction and returning whenever the work required their judgment.
I was elected to lead it.
The appointment required me to spend hundreds of years at a time in cryosuspension. I would sleep through epochs of construction, wake for major design reviews, inspect the work and approve the next phase.
The first hypershunt was already under construction when I accepted the appointment. It was intended to collect energy directly from a star and make that power available to automated construction systems far beyond any ordinary network.
The engineering difficulties were substantial.
The structure had to remain stable inside a star’s corona. Its collection systems had to survive constant radiation and violent changes in stellar activity. The transfer network had to carry more power in one moment than entire inhabited systems had ever consumed.
We lost dozens of unmanned assembly swarms before completing the first stable framework.
The second hypershunt was approved before the first reached full capacity. Its design incorporated everything we had learned. Construction proceeded more quickly, although centuries still passed outside my chamber.
Each waking period lasted several months, even years. I met engineers whose grandparents had worked under engineers I remembered. I approved changes to systems designed by people who had passed while I slept. The Domain expanded between each waking.
New systems joined the Gate network. Problems once considered impossible became trivial. I believed I was watching humanity mature, but I did not yet understand what was being lost.
When two hypershunts became operational, the Directorate approved the project they had been built to support.
I proposed the name Gan Eden, after the sacred garden of God.
It was to be the Domain’s first enclosed—
DOMAIN INFOSEC VIOLATION THRESHOLD WARNING
// datastream resetting...
—constructed around a yellow sun on the far outskirts of the Persean Sector. At its intended capacity, it could shelter several quintillion human li—
FATAL ACCESS ERROR //
This device is not authorized to provide additional description of the referenced project, destination, or design objective. Please upgrade your data permission level in compliance with Domain Information Security Standards.
I believed that the ability to construct such a wonder proved that the Domain deserved to continue expanding.
I was wrong.
entries.target:
已恢复的个人日志
作者：莱斯特，艾萨克·托马斯
文件：日志 — 第一部分
我的名字是艾萨克·托马斯·莱斯特，现任佩尔塞安星区日构系统公司的工程总监。
我的工作包括日冕超导分流器的建造，以及后来的伊甸园计划。
这些项目预计将耗时数个世纪。伊甸园计划可能需要超过一千年的时间才能达到最终的设计容量。 普通的行政管理层更替无法在如此漫长的时期内保存所需的技术知识、机构记忆和设计意图。
因此，人之领设立了延续办公室。 该办公室的主任将跨越数代履职，在主要建设阶段之间进入冷冻休眠状态，并在工程需要其判断时苏醒。
我被选中领导该办公室。
这一任命要求我每次在冷冻休眠状态中度过数百年。 我会睡过一个又一个建设时期，在重大设计审查时醒来，检查工程进度并批准下一阶段的工作。
当我接受这一任命时，第一条超空间分流通道已经开工建设。 其设计目的是直接从恒星收集能量，并将这种能量输送给远超普通网络范围的自动化建造系统。
工程上的困难相当大。
该结构必须在恒星日冕内保持稳定。 其能量采集系统必须能够承受持续辐射以及恒星活动剧烈变化。 传输网络必须在瞬间承载超过所有有人居住星系至今总能耗的能量。
在完成首个稳定框架前，我们损失了数十个无人组装群。
在首个超空间分流器达到满负荷前，第二个超空间分流器已获批准。 其设计融合了我们迄今所掌握的一切知识。尽管在我的密室之外，几个世纪依然流逝，但建设进度却更快了。
每次苏醒期都持续数月，甚至数年。我遇到了这样的工程师：他们的祖父母曾在我记忆中的工程师手下工作。 我批准了对那些在我沉睡期间已然离世的人所设计系统的修改。每次苏醒之间，人之领都在不断扩张。
新的系统加入了星门网络。 曾经被认为无法解决的问题变得微不足道。我以为自己正在见证人类的成长，却尚未明白正在失去什么。
当两条超空间短路通道投入运行时，总署批准了它们所支持的项目。
我提议将其命名为伊甸园，以纪念上帝的神圣花园。
这将作为人之领首个封闭式——
人之领 INFOSEC 违规阈值警告
// 数据流重置中……
——它围绕着佩尔塞亚星区最外缘的一颗黄色恒星建造而成。 按设计容量，它可容纳数千亿亿人类——
致命访问错误 //
本设备无权提供有关所引项目、目的地或设计目标的进一步说明。 请根据人之领信息安全标准升级您的数据权限级别。
我曾认为，能够建造如此奇迹的能力，证明了人之领值得继续扩张。
我是错的。

My name is Isaac Thomas Lester, currently serving as Director of Engineering at Helio Structural Systems in the Persean Sector.
My work includes the construction of the coronal superconducting shunt, as well as the subsequent Eden Project.
These projects are expected to span several centuries. The Eden Project may take over a thousand years to reach its final design capacity. Ordinary administrative turnover cannot preserve the necessary technical knowledge, institutional memory, and design intent over such an extended period.
Therefore, the Human Leadership established the Continuity Office. The director of this office will serve across generations, entering cryogenic hibernation between major construction phases and awakening when the project requires his judgment.
I have been selected to lead this office.
This appointment requires me to spend several hundred years in cryogenic hibernation at a time. I will sleep through one construction period after another, waking only during major design reviews to inspect project progress and approve the next phase of work.
When I accepted this appointment, construction had already begun on the first hyperspace bypass channel. It was designed to harvest energy directly from the star and transmit that energy to automated construction systems operating far beyond the reach of conventional networks.
The engineering challenges were considerable.
The structure must remain stable within the stellar corona. Its energy-harvesting system must withstand continuous radiation as well as drastic fluctuations in stellar activity. The transmission network must be capable of carrying, in an instant, more energy than the total energy consumption of all inhabited star systems to date.
Before completing the first stable framework, we lost dozens of unmanned assembly clusters.
Before the first hyperspace diverter reached full capacity, the second hyperspace diverter had already been approved. Its design incorporates all the knowledge we have acquired to date. Although centuries continued to pass outside my chamber, construction progressed at an accelerated pace.
Each period of awakening lasted months, even years. I encountered engineers whose grandparents had once worked under the engineers of my memory. I approved modifications to systems designed by those who had passed away during my slumber. Between each awakening, the Human Domain continued to expand.
New systems joined the Stargate Network. Problems once thought unsolvable became trivial. I believed I was witnessing humanity’s growth, yet I had not yet realized what I was losing.
When two hyperspace shortcut channels became operational, the General Administration approved the projects they supported.
I proposed naming it Eden, in honor of God’s sacred garden.
This will serve as the first enclosed—
DOMAIN INFOSEC Violation Threshold Warning
// Resetting data stream……
—it is constructed around a yellow star at the very outer edge of the Persea Star System. By design, it can accommodate hundreds of billions of humans—
Fatal Access Error //
This device is not authorized to provide further details regarding the referenced items, destinations, or design objectives. Please upgrade your data access level in accordance with the Human Domain’s information security standards.
I once believed that the ability to construct such a marvel proved the Human Domain was worthy of continued expansion.
I was wrong.

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART II
Before the continuity office was established, I lived at Telepylus Station with my wife, Rebecca Anne Sarai.
Rebecca was a senior engineer in stellar-transfer architecture. The Directorate offered us joint appointments: I as Director of the continuity office, Rebecca as its Chief Integration Engineer.
We intended to serve the entire tenure together, entering cryosuspension between construction phases and waking side by side whenever the work required us.
Our daughter was born shortly before the first long suspension interval. We placed her pediatric chamber beside our own, intending to wake and raise her during every active interval.
At the first scheduled revival, I woke.
Rebecca did not survive the thaw.
Complications from cryosuspension caused a permanent psychosomatic rupture. I had her euthanized the day I got the prognosis.
From then on, I accepted sole leadership, promising that I would finish the work and wake my daughter into the world Rebecca and I had intended for her.
I vowed to forever keep my daughter safe. Not until I, with my own hands, could ensure the world could not take her away from me like God did Rebecca.
I hate myself.
I hate myself.
I hate myself—

已恢复的个人日志
作者：莱斯特，艾萨克·托马斯
文件： 日志 — 第二部分
在延续办公室成立之前，我与妻子丽贝卡·安妮·萨拉伊居住在 Telepylus 空间站。
丽贝卡是恒星传输架构领域的高级工程师。 总署向我们提供了联合任命：我担任延续办公室主任，丽贝卡担任其首席集成工程师。
我们计划共同完成整个任期，在施工阶段之间进入低温休眠，并在工作需要时并肩苏醒。
我们的女儿在第一次长期休眠期开始前不久出生。 我们将她的儿童冷冻舱放在我们的冷冻舱旁边，打算在每个工作间隔期间唤醒她并抚养她长大。
在第一次预定的复苏时，我醒了。
丽贝卡在解冻过程中没有存活下来。
冷冻悬浮带来的并发症导致了永久性的心身功能紊乱。 得知预后当天，我安排了对她实施安乐死。
自那以后，我独自掌权，承诺完成任务，并在适当的时候唤醒女儿，让她进入丽贝卡和我曾为她规划的世界。
我发誓要永远保护女儿的安全。 除非我能亲手确保这个世界无法像上帝夺走丽贝卡那样，将她从我身边夺走。
我恨自己。
我恨自己。
我恨自己——

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART III
My daughter remained unchanged. I made certain of it.
At every waking, the physicians offered to revive her. At every waking, I refused. I visited her chamber, reviewed the medical reports, and repeated tests the technicians had already completed while centuries passed outside.
The Domain did not remain unchanged.
I saw a decay. The soul of Man gangrenous and rotting.
I met an Armada veteran cleaning coolant residue from a station floor. A reactor leak had destroyed half his face. His pension had been suspended because the archive containing his service record no longer existed.
I offered to help. He asked only that I help his daughter obtain a transit permit.
Seventy-two years passed. I never found out what happened to him or his daughter.
Nothing changed.
During another waking period, I met a woman who had spent years moving between ports because she could not obtain employment without proof of residence, or residence without proof of employment. The station classified her as a transient clearance burden.
Years blurred together. I can't tell if it was the repeated cryosuspensions or my deteriorating mind, but at some point I couldn't distinguish faces. I even forgot Rebecca's face.
I remembered the facts of her: the scar at her wrist, the hymn she hummed while she worked, the way she squeezed my hand when she was frightened. But whenever I tried to assemble those memories into a face, there was only an absence where my wife had been.
Rebecca.
You understood this before I did. You once told me that the Domain was the greatest work of man that had ever been made, and that was why it was so grotesque.
I began speaking publicly. At first, I presented reports and projections. The Directorate thanked me and established a commission.
Nothing changed.
I said that human beings were not obsolete machinery. I said that a civilization should be judged by those it could help and chose not to. I said that every person carried the image of God, whether or not the Domain could locate the correct record for them.
People began gathering to hear me. The gatherings became demonstrations. Security forces were deployed. People were injured, then killed.
I continued speaking, but I don't know why. With my mouth I drove lambs to the slaughter, and with my hands and my work I forged the knives the Domain of Man plunged into their necks.
Who was I?
No one. I was a worthless hypocrite.
I spoke out against the great Whore of Babylon whilst I remained her greatest slave.
Nothing changed.

已恢复的个人日志
作者：莱斯特，艾萨克·托马斯
文件：日志 — 第三部分
我的女儿依然如故。 我对此确信无疑。
每次她苏醒时，医生们都提议让她复活。每次她苏醒时，我都拒绝了。我前往她的病房，审阅医疗报告，并重复了技术人员早已完成的检测——而外界的时光却已流逝了几个世纪。
那人之领却并非一成不变。
我目睹了腐朽。人类的灵魂已如坏疽般腐烂。
我遇见了一位无畏舰队的老兵，他正在清理空间站地板上的冷却剂残留物。 反应堆泄漏毁掉了他半张脸。由于记录他服役经历的档案已不复存在，他的退休金被暂停发放。
我主动提出帮助。他只请求我协助他的女儿获得过境许可。
七十二年过去了。 我从未得知他和女儿的下落。
一切如故。
在又一次清醒期间，我遇到了一位女子，她多年来辗转于各个港口之间，因为没有居住证明就无法获得工作，而没有工作证明又无法获得居住许可。 车站将她归类为过境通关负担。
岁月模糊地交织在一起。我无法分辨是反复的冷冻休眠，还是我日渐衰退的思维所致，但不知从何时起，我已无法辨认面孔。 我甚至忘了丽贝卡的脸。
我记得关于她的细节：她手腕的疤痕，她工作时哼唱的赞美诗，以及她害怕时紧握我手的方式。 但每当我试图将这些记忆拼凑成一张脸时，我妻子曾经所在之处却只剩下一片空虚。
丽贝卡。
你比我更早明白了这一点。 你曾告诉我，人之领是人类有史以来最伟大的杰作，也正因如此，它才显得如此怪诞。
我开始公开发声。 起初，我只是提交报告和预测。总署向我表示感谢，并成立了一个委员会。
一切都没有改变。
我说，人类并非过时的机器。 我说，一个文明应当以其本可帮助却选择不帮助的对象来评判。我说，每个人都承载着上帝的形象，无论人之领能否为他们找到正确的记录。
人们开始聚集起来听我讲话。集会演变成了示威游行。安全部队被部署出来。 有人受伤，随后有人丧生。
我继续发言，但我不知道为什么。 我用嘴将羔羊驱向屠宰场，又用双手和我的劳动锻造出那些人之领刺入他们颈部的利刃。
我究竟是谁？
无人。 我不过是个一文不值的伪君子。
我高声谴责那大巴比伦的淫妇，而我却依然是她最忠实的奴隶。
一切都没有改变。

Author: Lester, Isaac Thomas
File: Log — Part Three
My daughter is still the same. I have no doubt about it.
Each time she woke up, the doctors suggested reviving her. Each time she woke up, I refused. I went to her ward, reviewed the medical reports, and repeated the tests the technicians had long since completed—while centuries had passed in the outside world.
Yet that person's essence is not static.
I have witnessed decay. The human soul has rotted like gangrene.
I met a veteran of the Fearless Fleet who was cleaning up coolant residue on the space station floor. A reactor leak had destroyed half his face. Since the records documenting his service no longer existed, his pension payments had been suspended.
I offered to help. He only asked me to assist his daughter in obtaining a transit permit.
Seventy-two years have passed. I never learned the whereabouts of him or his daughter.
Everything remains the same.
During another lucid moment, I met a woman who had been drifting from port to port for years—unable to find work without proof of residence, and unable to obtain a residence permit without proof of employment. The station classified her as a burden on transit clearance.
The years have blurred together. I cannot tell if it is due to repeated cryogenic hibernation or my increasingly failing mind, but at some point, I lost the ability to recognize faces. I have even forgotten Rebecca’s face.
I remember the details about her: the scar on her wrist, the hymns she hummed while working, and the way she clutched my hand when she was afraid. But whenever I try to piece these memories together into a face, there is only emptiness where my wife once was.
Rebecca.
You understood this before I did. You once told me that the Human Mind is humanity’s greatest masterpiece of all time, and that is precisely why it seems so bizarre.
I began to speak out publicly. At first, I simply submitted reports and forecasts. The General Administration thanked me and established a committee.
Nothing changed.
I said that humans are not obsolete machines. I said that a civilization should be judged by those it could have helped but chose not to. I said that every person bears the image of God, regardless of whether the Human Registry can find the correct records for them.
People began to gather to hear me speak. The gathering turned into a demonstration. Security forces were deployed. People were injured, and then people died.
I continued to speak, though I didn’t know why. With my mouth I drove the lambs to the slaughterhouse; with my hands and my labor I forged the sharp blades that the leaders plunged into their necks.
Who am I, after all?
No one. I am nothing but a worthless hypocrite.
I I loudly denounce the harlot of Babylon, yet I remain her most faithful slave.
Nothing has changed.

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART IV
The Domain arrested me for insurrection.
At trial, they presented my speeches, correspondence, and engineering reports. I denied very little. When the Sector Governor asked whether I recognized the absolute authority of the Domain of Man, I told him that all human authority was subordinate to God.
They found me guilty.
I was kept under house arrest at Telepylus Station while preparations were made to return me to Sol for sentencing. They still needed my knowledge of Gan Eden, and some of its oldest systems continued to recognize my credentials.
Finally, I decided to end it.
For the first time in centuries, I authorized my daughter’s revival. She was so small. I could nearly palm her in my hand. With hands shaking, I fashioned a small cradle from my old spacer suit. My only inheritence to my prodigal daughter. Then I re-suspended her. It felt like burying Rebecca all over again.
Then I set my plot in motion.
The hypershunts supplied Gan Eden through the Gate network. Their full output passed through the rings as energy before reaching the sphere’s master control system. I would sieze a craft, pass through the Penelope’s Star Gate, enter the control complex, and redirect the full output of both hypershunts into Gan Eden.
The Gan Eden would be destroyed, and I with it.
I escaped confinement, commandeered the transport, and changed its destination after the transit sequence began.
Telepylus security had already identified the ship, and I expected the escort to follow me through the Gate within seconds. Instead, the patrol craft broke formation before they reached the ring. Traffic control began issuing emergency orders over one another, several ships stopped answering, and the Gate-status displays failed in rapid succession.
I did not know what had drawn their attention away from me, only that the route to Gan Eden was still open. I entered the coordinates, drove the transport through at maximum thrust, and emerged into the restricted system without pursuit. Gan Eden’s control network accepted my credentials immediately. I seized the approach corridor and pushed the ship toward the master control complex before whatever was happening at Penelope’s Star could close the way behind me.
Oh, Hosanna. Hosaana in the higehest.
Despite its hubris and its separation from God, Gan Eden was the most beautiful place in the entire universe.
Once inside the system, I abandoned the transport and took a shuttle to the master control complex at the space elevator. For less than a second, the system behaved exactly as I had intended.
Then the Gate network began shutting down around me.
The conduits carrying the hypershunt output vanished before the power could reach Gan Eden. With nowhere else to go, the discharge collapsed back through the nearest ring still connected to the transfer system: Penelope’s Star.
I watched the impossibility of Adamantine shattering like clay over telemetry and break apart. A moment later, every other Gate disappeared from the network.
I intended to die in Gan Eden.
Instead, I was left alive inside it.

已恢复的个人日志
作者：莱斯特，艾萨克·托马斯
文件： 日志 — 第四部分
人之领以叛乱罪逮捕了我。
庭审时，他们出示了我的演讲稿、信件往来及工程报告。 我几乎没有否认什么。当分区总督问我是否承认人之领的绝对权威时，我告诉他，一切人类的权威都服从于上帝。
他们判定我有罪。
在准备将我送回索尔接受宣判期间，我被软禁在 Telepylus 空间站。 他们仍需要我对伊甸园的了解，而且那里的部分最古老系统仍认可我的资质。
最后，我决定结束这一切。
几个世纪以来，我第一次授权让我的女儿复活。她那么小。 几乎可以整个人捧在手心。我双手颤抖着，用那套旧的太空服为她制作了一个小小的摇篮。这是我留给这个浪子女儿的唯一遗产。随后，我将她重新置入休眠状态。那种感觉，仿佛又在埋葬一次丽贝卡。
随后，我开始实施我的计划。
超空间分流器通过星门网络向伊甸园供能。它们的全部输出以能量形式穿过环带，最终抵达球体的总控制系统。 我将劫持一艘飞船，穿过 Penelope's Star 星门，进入控制中心，并将两条超空间分流器的全部输出重定向至伊甸园。
伊甸园将被摧毁，而我也将随之毁灭。
我逃离了软禁，强行接管运输船，并在传送序列启动后更改目的地。
Telepylus 安全部门早已识别出这艘飞船，我预计护航舰队将在数秒内通过星门追击。 然而，巡逻舰在抵达环形结构之前就打破了队形。 交通管制中心开始互相争相发布紧急命令，几艘飞船停止了应答，星门状态显示屏也接连失灵。
我不知道是什么转移了他们的注意力，只知道通往伊甸园的航线仍然畅通。 我输入坐标，以最大推力驾驶运输船穿过星门，在无人追击的情况下进入了该限制星系。伊甸园的控制网络立即接受了我的身份认证。我迅速进入进近航道，在 Penelope's Star 发生的一切事件封锁我身后通道之前，将飞船驶向主控制中心。
哦，和撒那。至高无上的和撒那。
尽管伊甸园充满傲慢且与上帝疏离，但它仍是整个宇宙中最美丽的地方。
进入该星系后，我弃用运输船，转乘一艘穿梭机前往太空电梯旁的主控制中心。 不到一秒钟，系统完全按照我的预期运行。
随后，我周围的星门网络开始关闭。
传输超空间分流输出的管道在能量抵达伊甸园之前便已消失。 无处可去，放电流倒灌回了仍与传输系统相连的最近环状结构：Penelope's Star。
我通过遥测数据目睹了本应坚不可摧之物如黏土般碎裂崩解。 片刻之后，网络中其余所有的星门都消失了。
我本打算在伊甸园里死去。
然而，我却活了下来，被困在其中。

Author: Lester, Isaac Thomas
File: Log — Part Four
The Human Domain arrested me on charges of rebellion.
During the trial, they presented my speeches, correspondence, and engineering reports. I denied almost nothing. When the Sector Governor asked me if I acknowledged the absolute authority of the Human Domain, I told him that all human authority is subject to God.
They found me guilty.
While preparations were being made to send me back to Sol to face sentencing, I was placed under house arrest at the Taylor-Pilus Station. They still needed my knowledge of Eden, and some of the oldest systems there still recognized my credentials.
Finally, I decided to put an end to it all.
For the first time in centuries, I authorized the resurrection of my daughter. She was so small. I could almost hold her entire body in the palm of my hand. With trembling hands, I fashioned a tiny cradle for her out of that old spacesuit. It was the only legacy I left for this wayward daughter of mine. Afterward, I placed her back into stasis. It felt as though I were burying Rebecca all over again.
Then I began to carry out my plan.
The hyperspace diverters supply power to Eden through the Stargate network. Their entire output travels through the ring in the form of energy, eventually reaching the sphere’s central control system. I will hijack a starship, pass through the Penelope Star Stargate, enter the control center, and redirect the full output of both hyperspace diverters to Eden.
Eden will be destroyed, and I will perish along with it.
I escaped house arrest, forcibly took control of a transport ship, and altered its destination after the jump sequence had been initiated.
Taylor-Pilus Security has already identified this ship, and I expect the escort fleet to pursue me through the Stargate within seconds. However, the patrol ships broke formation before reaching the ring structure. The traffic control centers began scrambling to issue emergency orders; several ships ceased responding, and the Stargate status displays failed one after another.
I do not know what diverted their attention, only that the route to Eden remains clear. I entered the coordinates and piloted the transport ship through the stargate at maximum thrust, entering the restricted system without being pursued. Eden’s control network immediately accepted my authentication. I quickly entered the approach lane and steered the ship toward the main control center before the events unfolding on Penelope’s Star blocked the passage behind me.
Oh, Hallelujah. Supreme Hallelujah.
Despite Eden’s arrogance and estrangement from God, it remains the most beautiful place in the entire universe.
Upon entering the star system, I jettisoned the transport ship and boarded a shuttle to the main control center next to the space elevator. In less than a second, the system operated exactly as I had anticipated.
Shortly thereafter, the Stargate network around me began to shut down.
The conduits transmitting the hyperspace bypass output vanished before the energy could reach Eden. With nowhere else to go, the current surged back into the nearest ring structure still connected to the transmission system: Penelope’s Star.
Through telemetry data, I witnessed the indestructible Adamantine shatter and crumble like clay. Moments later, all other Stargates in the network vanished.
I had intended to die in Eden.
However, I survived—and found myself trapped there.

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — FINAL
I am dying.
I have lived alone in Gan Eden for thirty-six years.
I spent the first several years searching the cities, shelters, maintenance tunnels, and transit stations. I transmitted on every emergency frequency that still worked.
No one answered. I knew no one would. The last human technicians had left Gan Eden centuries before, when its construction passed entirely to the automated swarms. I was the one who signed off on that order.
I eventually settled in this place I named Galilee, repaired one of the old agricultural houses, and learned to farm. When I was not working, I wandered the shell. I walked through empty cities, forests planted by machines, and coastlines no human being had ever seen. It is a never-ending day here, as if it were before God separated Light from Darkness.
Gan Eden remained beautiful.
Oh, God.
I also continued trying to restore the Gate connection to Penelope’s Star. At first, I told myself I was trying to rescue my daughter. I admit now that I only want to know whether I killed her.
Oh, my daughter.
Rebecca wanted to name you Leah.
To Leah, my beautiful daughter I never knew:
I said I saved you for a future I believed I could build. That was only partly true.
Every physician told me you could be revived. Every report said your chamber was sound. But whenever I imagined authorizing the thaw, I saw Rebecca dying on the revival table. I kept you asleep because I was afraid.
I dressed that fear in duty and chased my arrogant dream across centuries. Then, when the world failed to become what I envisioned, I abandoned you to your fate.
Neither you nor God owe me any forgiveness.
I prayed for you every day. I prayed for Rebecca. I prayed for the dead, and for the living I had condemned without ever knowing their names.
I do not know whether God heard me.
Until today.
Today, God finally answered.
It did not connect to Penelope’s Star or any other Gate I knew. Instead, two angels arrived through the the Earth and began ascending toward the Space Elevator.
The first resembles a winged figure, though my instruments cannot hold its shape for more than a moment. The second turns within lines of fire like a burning sword. They burn with the light of God and race through the sky like searing chariots.
I have named them Cherubim and the Lahat Ha-cherev.
Surely the Lord has sent them down here as gatekeepers of a false paradise. I foolishly attempted to pass by their contempous gaze, but God sees all.
Leah, I hope someone found you.
I hope they gave you a life beyond mine, and a name that belonged to you. I hope you were raised by people who loved you without asking you to carry their grief, their faith, or their failures. I hope that when you looked toward the future, you saw something of your own choosing rather than the ruins of what I had planned for you.
I hope you laughed every day. I hope you were stubborn like Rebecca. I hope you were kinder than I became. I hope you found love in this world, children of your own, and a home. I hope you found the blessings of God beneath these infinite heavens.
I hope that one day you know this:
I love you, Leah.
Isaac Thomas Leicester.
entries.target:
已恢复的个人日志
作者：莱斯特，艾萨克·托马斯
文件： 日志 — 最终版
我快死了。
我在伊甸园独居了三十六年。
最初的几年里，我搜遍了城市、避难所、维护隧道和交通枢纽。我尝试了所有还能使用的紧急频率进行呼叫。
却无人应答。我知道不会有人回应。 最后一批人类技术人员早在几个世纪前就离开了伊甸园，那时这里的建设工作已完全交由自动化群落负责。签署那道命令的正是我。
我最终定居于此——我将这里命名为加利利，修缮了一座旧农舍，并学会了务农。 闲暇时，我便在星壳中漫游。我穿行于空荡的城市、机器栽种的森林，以及人类从未见过的海岸线之间。这里永远是白天，仿佛还处于上帝尚未将光与暗分开的时期。
伊甸园依然美丽。
哦，上帝。
我也一直在尝试恢复通往 Penelope's Star 的星门连接。起初，我告诉自己这是为了营救我的女儿。 如今我承认，我只是想知道是否是我亲手害死了她。
哦，我的女儿。
丽贝卡原本想给你取名叫莉亚。
致莉亚，我从未谋面的美丽女儿：
我说过，我是为了一个我相信自己能够构建的未来而把你保存下来的。但这只说对了一半。
每一位医生都告诉我，你可以被复苏。 每份报告都显示你的冷冻舱完好无损。但每当我想象下令解冻时，我便看见丽贝卡在复苏台上死去。我让你一直沉睡，只因我害怕。
我将这份恐惧包装成责任，并追逐着我那狂妄的梦想跨越了几个世纪。 后来，当世界未能成为我想象中的模样时，我便将你弃之不顾，任其自生自灭。
无论是你，还是上帝，都不欠我任何宽恕。
我每天都在为你祈祷。 我为丽贝卡祈祷。我为逝者祈祷，也为那些我从未知晓姓名却已判处死刑的生者祈祷。
我不知道上帝是否听见了我的祈祷。
直到今天。
今天，上帝终于作出了回应。
它并没有连接到 Penelope's Star，也没有连接到我所知的任何其他星门。 取而代之的是，两名天使穿过大地降临，并开始朝太空电梯升去。
第一位形似有翼之姿，尽管我的仪器无法将其形态捕捉超过一瞬间。 第二个则在火线之中盘旋，宛如一把燃烧的宝剑。它们燃烧着上帝之光，如灼热的战车般疾驰于天际。
我将他们命名为 Cherubim 和 拉哈特·哈-切雷夫。
主无疑是派他们来到这里，作为这个虚假乐园的守门人。 我曾愚蠢地试图从它们轻蔑的目光下溜走，但上帝无所不见。
莉亚，我希望有人找到了你。
我希望他们给了你比我更美好的生活，以及一个真正属于你的名字。 我希望你被那些爱你的人抚养长大，他们不会要求你背负他们的悲伤、信仰或失败。我希望当你展望未来时，看到的是你自己选择的道路，而不是我为你规划的那片废墟。
我希望你每天都能开怀大笑。 我希望你像丽贝卡一样倔强。我希望你比我后来变得更善良。我希望你在这个世界上找到了爱、自己的孩子，以及一个家。 我希望你能在这无垠的苍穹之下，感受到上帝的恩典。
我希望有一天你能明白这一点：
我爱你，莉亚。
艾萨克·托马斯·莱斯特。
entries.backTranslation:
Restored Personal Log
Author: Lester, Isaac Thomas
File: Log — Final Version
I’m dying.
I have lived alone in Eden for thirty-six years.
During the first few years, I scoured the city, shelters, maintenance tunnels, and transportation hubs. I tried calling on every emergency frequency that was still operational.
But no one answered. I knew no one would respond. The last human technicians left Eden centuries ago, when construction work here was fully handed over to automated colonies. I was the one who signed that order.
I eventually settled here—I named this place Galilee, restored an old farmhouse, and learned to farm. In my spare time, I wandered through the Star Shell. I wandered through deserted cities, machine-planted forests, and coastlines that humans had never seen. It was always daytime here, as if we were still in the time before God had separated light from darkness.
Eden is still beautiful.
Oh, God.
I’ve also been trying to restore the Stargate connection to the Star of Penelope. At first, I told myself it was to rescue my daughter. Now I admit that I just want to know if I was the one who killed her with my own hands.
Oh, my daughter.
Rebecca had intended to name you Leah.
To Leia, my beautiful daughter whom I’ve never met:
I said I preserved you for a future I believed I could build. But that was only half the truth.
Every doctor told me you could be revived. Every report showed your cryochamber was intact. But whenever I imagined giving the order to thaw you, I saw Rebecca dying on the revival table. I kept you in a deep sleep simply because I was afraid.
I disguised that fear as a sense of duty and pursued my arrogant dream across the centuries. Later, when the world failed to turn out the way I’d imagined, I abandoned you, leaving you to fend for yourself.
Neither you nor God owes me any forgiveness.
I pray for you every day. I pray for Rebecca. I pray for the dead, and I pray for the living—those whose names I’ve never known but who have already been sentenced to death.
I don’t know if God has heard my prayers.
Until today.
Today, God has finally answered.
It did not connect to the Star of Penelope, nor to any other stargate I know of. Instead, two angels descended through the earth and began ascending toward the space elevator.
The first appeared to have wings, though my instruments could not capture its form for more than a fleeting moment. The second soared amid a trail of fire, like a blazing sword. They burned with the light of God, racing across the sky like scorching war chariots.
I named them Cherubim and Rahat Ha-Cherev.
The Lord has undoubtedly sent them here to serve as gatekeepers of this false paradise. I foolishly tried to slip away from their scornful gaze, but God sees all.
Leia, I hope someone has found you.
I hope they’ve given you a better life than I could, and a name that truly belongs to you. I hope you’ve been raised by people who love you—people who won’t ask you to carry their sorrow, their beliefs, or their failures. I hope that when you look to the future, you see the path you’ve chosen for yourself, not the ruins I mapped out for you.
I hope you laugh heartily every day. I hope you are as stubborn as Rebecca. I hope you grow to be kinder than I eventually became. I hope you find love, children of your own, and a home in this world. I hope you can feel God's grace beneath this boundless sky.
I hope that one day you’ll understand this:
I love you, Leah.
Isaac Thomas Lester.
